teile.einleitung: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean and a country with around 10 million inhabitants. It has been governed by communists since the revolution of 1959. Cuba is known for colourful vintage cars, music, cigars and its long dispute with the USA.
wichtigste: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean, and its capital is Havana.
A communist party has governed there since the revolution of 1959.
The leaders of the revolution were Fidel Castro and Che Guevara.
In 1962 the Cuban Missile Crisis brought the world to the brink of nuclear war.
From 1960 the USA imposed a trade embargo on Cuba.
From 1961 to 2015 Switzerland represented the interests of the USA in Cuba.
People in Cuba speak Spanish.

abschnitte.text: Cuba lies in the Caribbean Sea, only about 150 kilometres south of Florida in the USA. The main island is about 1,250 kilometres long and narrow. There are sandy beaches, coral reefs, tobacco fields and mountains such as the **Sierra Maestra**. The climate is tropically warm, and from June to November there is a risk of hurricanes.

Before 1959 the dictator **Fulgencio Batista** ruled, supported by the USA. Rebels led by **Fidel Castro** and the Argentinian Che Guevara fought against him from the mountains of the Sierra Maestra. On 1 January 1959 Batista fled, and the rebels took power. Castro soon nationalised companies and land and allied himself with the Soviet Union.

In 1961 an attack by Cuban exiles supported by the USA failed at the **Bay of Pigs**. In 1962 the Soviet Union secretly set up nuclear missiles in Cuba, which led to the **Cuban Missile Crisis**. After thirteen dangerous days the missiles were withdrawn again. The US trade embargo still exists today.

Fidel Castro ruled for almost 50 years, then his brother Raúl took over, and since 2019 Miguel Díaz-Canel has been president. Schools and healthcare are free, and Cuba has many doctors. At the same time there is poverty, power cuts and a shortage of food, and there are no free elections. In recent years a great many people have emigrated.

Cuba is famous for music such as **salsa** and son, and for cigars, rum and sugar cane. In Havana many American cars from the 1950s are still driving around. The old town of Havana is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. From 1961 to 2015 Switzerland was the **protecting power** for the USA in Cuba, because the two countries had no embassies in each other's country.

begriffe.erklaerung: A rapid, often violent overthrow of the government.
A ban on trading with a country.
A dangerous dispute in 1962 over Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba.
A country that represents the interests of another country in a third country.

gewusst: Because hardly any new cars could be imported, Cubans have been repairing their old vintage cars with great ingenuity for decades.
The smallest bird in the world, the bee hummingbird, lives in Cuba.

teile.einleitung: The Communist Party of China has governed the People's Republic of China as the only party since 1949. With about 100 million members it is one of the largest parties in the world. It controls politics, the economy and the media in this populous country.
wichtigste: China is the largest country in which a communist party still governs alone today.
The party was founded in Shanghai in 1921.
Its best-known leader was Mao Zedong, who proclaimed the People's Republic in 1949.
From 1978 Deng Xiaoping opened the economy to markets and trade.
Since 2012 Xi Jinping has been general secretary of the party.
In 2024 the party had about 100 million members.
Other parties may not challenge its power, and criticism is strictly controlled.

abschnitte.text: The party was founded in **Shanghai** in July 1921 by a small group that included Mao Zedong. For a long time it fought against the nationalist Kuomintang. During the **Long March** in 1934 and 1935, the Red Army fled thousands of kilometres across China. After winning the civil war, Mao proclaimed the People's Republic of China on 1 October 1949.

Under Mao the party tried to transform China quickly. During the “Great Leap Forward” from 1958 there was a famine in which many millions died. From 1966 to 1976 came the **Cultural Revolution**, with a great deal of violence and chaos. The party itself later described this period as a great mistake.

After Mao's death in 1976, **Deng Xiaoping** came out on top. From 1978 he allowed private companies, trade with other countries and markets. As a result China became one of the world's largest economic powers. Politically, however, everything stayed with the party; in 1989 it had the protests on Tiananmen Square in Beijing ended by force.

A **party congress** takes place every five years, most recently the 20th Party Congress in 2022. The greatest power lies with the Standing Committee of the Politburo, which has seven members. At the top is the **general secretary**, since 2012 Xi Jinping, who is also president of the state. The party has groups in companies, schools, universities and the military.

The party controls newspapers, television and the internet, and many Western websites are blocked in China. Human rights organisations criticise its treatment of minorities such as the Uyghurs and Tibetans. At the same time China is an important trading partner for many countries. In 2013 Switzerland was one of the first European countries to sign a **free trade agreement** with China.

begriffe.erklaerung: The top leader of the party.
The small group of the most powerful party leaders.
A large meeting at which the party decides on its leadership and goals.
The retreat of the communist army across China in 1934 and 1935.

gewusst: With around 100 million members, the party has more members than Germany has inhabitants.
A huge picture of Mao Zedong still hangs on the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing today.

t1yclwcn.t: Communist Party of the Soviet Union

teile.einleitung: The Communist Party of the Soviet Union, CPSU for short, was the only party allowed in the Soviet Union. From 1917 to 1991 it decided almost everything in the huge country. Its leaders, the general secretaries, were the most powerful people in the state.
wichtigste: The CPSU was the only party allowed in the Soviet Union.
It grew out of the Bolsheviks under Lenin.
The name CPSU was used from 1952; before that it had other names.
The general secretary was the real ruler of the country.
Well-known party leaders were Stalin, Khrushchev, Brezhnev and Gorbachev.
In the 1980s it had almost 19 million members.
After the attempted coup in 1991 the party was banned, and shortly afterwards the Soviet Union broke up.

abschnitte.text: The party grew out of the **Bolsheviks**, a group of Russian socialists under Lenin. They split from more moderate socialists in 1903. With the October Revolution of 1917 they took power in Russia. After that the party changed its name several times; from 1952 it was called the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

No other party was allowed to exist in the Soviet Union. At the top were the **Politburo** and the **general secretary**. The party decided about the government, the army, the economy, schools and newspapers. Party membership was almost always necessary for a good career.

After Lenin, **Joseph Stalin** ruled with great harshness from the 1920s until his death in 1953. He was followed by Nikita Khrushchev and, from 1964, by Leonid Brezhnev. After short periods under Yuri Andropov and Konstantin Chernenko, Mikhail Gorbachev became general secretary in 1985. He tried to renew the country with reforms.

Under Stalin the party had millions of people persecuted, and many were sent to the labour camps of the **Gulag**. Even many party members were killed in the purges of the 1930s. Later too, critics were locked up or put in psychiatric hospitals. The secret police, the KGB, served the party as its tool.

In August 1991 old party leaders tried to stop Gorbachev's reforms with a coup. The coup failed after three days, partly because of the resistance led by Boris Yeltsin. After that the activities of the CPSU were banned. In December 1991 the **Soviet Union** dissolved, and 15 new states came into being.

begriffe.erklaerung: The group around Lenin from which the party emerged; the word means “members of the majority”.
The small, most powerful leadership body of the party.
The system of labour camps in the Soviet Union.
An attempt to overthrow the government by force.

gewusst: The Kremlin in Moscow was the seat of the party leadership and is today the seat of the Russian president.
Gorbachev was the only general secretary who was also elected President of the Soviet Union by parliament.

teile.einleitung: The Korean War lasted from 1950 to 1953 and was one of the first big wars of the Cold War. Communist North Korea attacked the south in order to unite the country. To this day there is no peace treaty, and Swiss officers still monitor the ceasefire.
wichtigste: On 25 June 1950 North Korea attacked South Korea.
The aim was to unite all of Korea under communist rule.
United Nations troops led by the USA helped South Korea.
From the autumn of 1950 China sent hundreds of thousands of soldiers to support the north.
On 27 July 1953 a ceasefire was signed in Panmunjom.
Millions of people died, including a great many civilians.
Switzerland is still part of the commission that monitors the ceasefire today.

abschnitte.text: From 1910 to 1945 Korea was a Japanese colony. After the Second World War the country was divided at the **38th parallel**. The Soviet Union occupied the north and the USA the south. In 1948 two states were formed, in the north under Kim Il-sung and in the south under Syngman Rhee.

On 25 June 1950 North Korean troops crossed the border. Within a few days they captured the capital, **Seoul**. The South Koreans were pushed back into a small corner around the city of Busan. The **United Nations** decided to help South Korea with troops from many countries.

abschnitte.titel: Back and forth at the front
abschnitte.text: In September 1950 UN troops under General Douglas MacArthur landed at **Incheon**, behind the North Koreans. They pushed the north back almost to the Chinese border. Then China intervened with hundreds of thousands of soldiers. After that the front stayed roughly at the 38th parallel for a long time.

After two years of negotiations a ceasefire was signed in **Panmunjom** on 27 July 1953. A peace treaty never followed, so legally the war has not ended. Since then a **demilitarised zone** about 4 kilometres wide has separated the two states. It is one of the most heavily guarded borders in the world.

An estimated several million people died in the war, many cities were destroyed, and families were separated for decades. Korea is still divided today; the south became a democracy and the north remained a dictatorship. Since 1953 Switzerland and Sweden have formed the **Neutral Nations Supervisory Commission**. To this day, members of the Swiss army serve there in Panmunjom.

begriffe.erklaerung: The fighting stops, but there is not yet a proper peace.
An imaginary line on the globe along which Korea was divided in 1945.
A border strip in which no army may be stationed.
The UN, a community of almost all the states in the world.

gewusst: The Korean War is sometimes called the “forgotten war”, because it is less well known in the West than other wars.
The Swiss delegation in Korea is the Swiss army's oldest mission abroad.

teile.einleitung: A communist party is a party that campaigns for the ideas of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. In some countries such a party governs on its own. In Switzerland there are small left-wing parties that are close to these ideas.
wichtigste: Communist parties refer to Marx and Engels.
In the Soviet Union only the Communist Party was allowed to govern.
China has been governed by the Communist Party since 1949 (as of 2026).
Cuba is also governed by a Communist Party (as of 2026).
The Communist Party of Switzerland was founded in 1921.
The Party of Labour (PdA) was founded in 1944.
The best-known song of the communists is called “The Internationale”.

abschnitte.text: In 1848 **Karl Marx** and **Friedrich Engels** wrote the **“Manifesto of the Communist Party”**. In it they called for a society in which factories and land belong to everyone together. Parties that want to achieve this call themselves a **communist party**. Their best-known song is **“The Internationale”**. From 1922 to 1944 it was even the anthem of the Soviet Union.

In the **Soviet Union** only the Communist Party had power. Other parties were banned. This is called a **one-party state**. So in elections people could hardly **choose between parties**. There was no real choice, and criticising the party was dangerous.

In **China** the **Communist Party of China** has governed alone since **1949** (as of 2026). Other parties may not compete for power. In **Cuba** in the Caribbean too, a communist party has governed since the revolution of **1959**. For a long time **Fidel Castro** was the leader there; he ruled for almost 50 years. Other examples are Vietnam and Laos.

The **Communist Party of Switzerland** was founded in **1921**. It always remained a small party and was banned in 1940. In **1944** the **Party of Labour**, **PdA** for short, was founded. It is close to the ideas of communism and is also small. In Switzerland people can choose between **many parties** in elections.

gewusst: The “Manifesto of the Communist Party” was published in London in 1848.
The words of “The Internationale” were written by the Frenchman Eugène Pottier in 1871.

teile.einleitung: The Yalta Conference was a meeting of the three most important Allies in February 1945. Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin discussed what should happen after the victory over Germany. Their decisions shaped Europe for decades.
wichtigste: The conference took place from 4 to 11 February 1945.
Yalta is on the Crimean peninsula on the Black Sea.
Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin are called the “Big Three”.
Germany was to be divided into occupation zones.
Stalin promised to enter the war against Japan.
The founding of the United Nations was prepared.
The Potsdam Conference followed in the summer of 1945.

abschnitte.text: Yalta is a resort on the southern coast of the **Crimean** peninsula on the **Black Sea**. The conference met in the **Livadia Palace** from **4 to 11 February 1945**. The Second World War in Europe was almost over at that time. The Allied troops were advancing on Germany from the west and the east.

At Yalta **Franklin D. Roosevelt** met for the USA, **Winston Churchill** for Great Britain and **Joseph Stalin** for the Soviet Union. They are called the **“Big Three”**. Although they were fighting Germany together, they had different aims. The Western states wanted democracy, while Stalin wanted to secure the Soviet Union's influence in Eastern Europe.

The Allies decided to divide Germany into **occupation zones** after the victory. **France** was also to receive its own zone. **Poland's** borders were to be moved **westwards**. The Soviet Union kept eastern Poland. In compensation, Poland was to receive territory in the west at Germany's expense.

**Stalin** promised to fight against **Japan** three months after the end of the war in Europe. In **August 1945** the Soviet Union did indeed declare war on Japan. The three powers also prepared the **United Nations**. They agreed on a founding conference in **San Francisco**, where the UN Charter was signed in June 1945.

Roosevelt died in April 1945. So at the **Potsdam Conference** near Berlin in July and August 1945, **Harry S. Truman** represented the USA. Many people see Yalta as a beginning of the division of Europe into East and West. This division lasted throughout the **Cold War**.

gewusst: The Livadia Palace used to be a summer residence of the Russian tsars.
Roosevelt was already seriously ill at the conference and died two months later.

teile.einleitung: On 13 December 1981 Poland's communist leadership under General Wojciech Jaruzelski imposed martial law. Its main aim was to crush the independent trade union Solidarność. Martial law officially lasted until 1983.
wichtigste: Martial law was declared during the night of 12 to 13 December 1981.
Power was held by the Military Council of National Salvation under Jaruzelski.
The trade union Solidarność was suspended and banned in 1982.
Lech Wałęsa was interned for about eleven months.
At the Wujek coal mine, nine striking miners were shot dead.
On 22 July 1983 martial law was formally lifted.

abschnitte.text: During the night of **13 December 1981** the Polish leadership imposed **martial law**. Tanks appeared in the streets, telephone lines were cut and there was a curfew. **Thousands of opposition members** were arrested and **interned**, that is, locked up without trial. Power was held by the **Military Council of National Salvation**, **WRON** in Polish. It was made up of senior officers under General **Wojciech Jaruzelski**.

Martial law was directed above all against the trade union **Solidarność**. It was independent of the state and had around **ten million** members. With martial law it was suspended and officially banned in **1982**. Its leader **Lech Wałęsa** was arrested on the very first night. He remained interned until **14 November 1982**.

Many workers went on strike against martial law. On **16 December 1981** special police units opened fire on striking miners at the **Wujek mine** in **Katowice**. **Nine people** died. It was the bloodiest incident during martial law. Today a large cross there commemorates the victims.

At Christmas 1981 US President **Ronald Reagan** called on people to put a **candle in the window** as a sign of solidarity with Poland. The USA also imposed **sanctions**. At the end of 1982 martial law was suspended, and on **22 July 1983** it was formally lifted. Jaruzelski later said it had been a **“lesser evil”**, because it had prevented an invasion by the Soviet Union. Whether this danger really existed is **disputed** among historians.

gewusst: On the morning of 13 December 1981, Polish television showed a speech by Jaruzelski instead of its usual programmes.
Many restrictions from the time of martial law remained in the laws even after 1983.

teile.einleitung: War communism is the name for the economic policy of the Bolsheviks in Russia during the civil war, from about 1918 to 1921. The state took over industry and forced the peasants to hand over grain. The results were hunger and a lot of unrest.
wichtigste: War communism lasted from about 1918 to 1921.
From June 1918 large-scale industry was nationalised.
Peasants had to hand over grain by force; this was called prodrazvyorstka.
Armed food detachments seized grain in the countryside.
Because of inflation, workers were often paid in food instead of money.
Private trade was banned; black marketeers were called meshochniki.
In 1921 war communism was replaced by the New Economic Policy.

abschnitte.text: After the October Revolution of 1917, **civil war** broke out in Russia. The Bolsheviks wanted to run the economy entirely from the state. With a decree of **28 June 1918** the large industrial enterprises were **nationalised**. By 1920 many small enterprises had also come into state hands. The state banned **private trade**.

The cities and the army needed food. Under **prodrazvyorstka** the state set how much grain each region had to hand over. Armed **food detachments** made up of workers went into the villages and took the grain by force. Often they even took the peasants' **seed grain**. From June 1918 **Committees of the Village Poor** were meant to mobilise poor peasants against better-off ones. Because they divided the villages, they were dissolved at the end of 1918.

Because of **inflation**, paper money lost almost all its value. So workers were increasingly paid **in kind**, for example in food rations. Many town dwellers went hungry. The **meshochniki** illegally brought food in sacks from the countryside to the towns. Their name comes from the Russian word for sack.

In 1920 **Leon Trotsky** proposed militarising labour and forming **labour armies** from troops that were no longer needed. But discontent grew: peasants rose up, and in 1921 the **Kronstadt sailors' rebellion** broke out. The party under **Lenin** then decided on the **New Economic Policy** in 1921. It allowed some trade again and replaced the compulsory handing over of grain with a tax.

gewusst: The New Economic Policy is often abbreviated to NEP.
Because of the hunger, many people moved from the towns back to the countryside.

teile.einleitung: In March 1921 the sailors of the fortress of Kronstadt rose up against Bolshevik rule. They demanded free elections to the soviets and more freedoms. The Red Army crushed the uprising after a few weeks.
wichtigste: Kronstadt is on Kotlin Island in the Gulf of Finland, off St Petersburg.
In 1917 the Kronstadt sailors were seen as especially revolutionary.
They adopted their resolution on the battleship Petropavlovsk.
They demanded new elections to the soviets by secret ballot.
Stepan Petrichenko led the rebels' Revolutionary Committee.
Mikhail Tukhachevsky led the assault across the ice.
Kronstadt fell on 18 March 1921.

abschnitte.text: Kronstadt is on **Kotlin** Island in the **Gulf of Finland**, off **St Petersburg**. **Peter the Great** had the island fortified as a naval base. During the revolution of **1917**, the Kronstadt sailors were seen as especially revolutionary. At that time **Leon Trotsky** praised them as the **“pride and glory of the revolution”**.

After the civil war there was hunger and great hardship in Russia. At the end of **February 1921** the sailors on the battleship **Petropavlovsk** adopted a **resolution**. They demanded **new elections to the soviets by secret ballot**, as well as freedom of speech and of the press for left-wing parties. They wanted to free the councils from the rule of the party. The resolution became the programme of the uprising.

The rebels formed a **Provisional Revolutionary Committee**. It was led by **Stepan Petrichenko**, a clerk on the Petropavlovsk. The Bolsheviks saw the uprising as a threat to their power. The fact that it was the Kronstadt sailors of all people who rose up hit them especially hard.

In March the sea around Kronstadt was still **frozen**. Soldiers of the **Red Army** in white camouflage capes stormed **across the open ice**. The attack was led by **Mikhail Tukhachevsky** with the 7th Army. After heavy losses on both sides, Kronstadt fell on **18 March 1921**. Petrichenko fled abroad, and many other rebels were harshly punished.

gewusst: At the same time as the uprising, the party decided on the New Economic Policy and relaxed its control of the economy.
Today Kronstadt is part of the city of St Petersburg.
